findings.description: The KMS key used to encrypt the audit trail bucket does not set enable_key_rotation = true, so the customer-managed key material is never automatically rotated. CIS AWS Foundations requires rotation to be enabled for customer-managed CMKs, which limits the amount of data exposed by a single compromised key.

No policy argument is supplied, so AWS applies the default key policy that delegates full kms:* access to the account root, allowing any IAM principal in the account with sufficient IAM permissions to use or administer the audit trail key. An explicit least-privilege key policy should scope usage to the audit logging service and specific administrators.
